content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm encountering a strange problem when trying to connect to my [product_name] web server ([version_no], latest version). I followed the procedure to enable the web server, and initially, everything worked fine. I could access the web server using a link I set up on my computer and smartphone. [url] After a few successful connections, I receive an 'Error 403: The target is forbidden.' If I install a new web browser, it works briefly before failing again. I suspect it might be an issue with my shortcut, but I'm not certain. Any suggestions? For reference, ping works consistently and my IP address is nearly static since my router rarely disconnects.
Dear [user_name], Unfortunately, we do not know the exact reason for this message. You might find assistance at the following link: [url] Best regards, [company_name] Support

The issue could be related to the IP not being released properly after the previous connection. I faced a similar problem and resolved it by changing the IP and downloading to the controller; it worked with the new IP. However, I did not try using the public address function as you described, so cannot comment on that specifically. It's important to ensure that the previous session via the web server is closed properly. Another suggestion is to use a different browser and see if the problem persists. I was sometimes able to access using Internet Explorer, but not with Google Chrome. Hope this helps.

Hi, I experienced a similar issue when using Chrome; Firefox and Internet Explorer were fine, but Chrome caused a 403 error. After deleting all cookies and browser data in Chrome, it worked again. Regards, [user_name]
I encountered a similar issue and discovered that the port should be set to 8000, not 8080, which is used only for programming by [product_name] software.
That information isn't accurate. Please refer to the attachment.

Thank you. However, I am experiencing issues with port 8080 when accessing through free DNS NO-IP.com. Port 8000 is working fine; perhaps there's confusion in the router's port forwarding configuration on my end. I'll review my setup again. Appreciate your help.
Hello, Can you please share the specific solution that resolved your issue?

Hi! In my case, the issue was that I hadn't set up a login page. I received this error when accessing the page directly via a link, and it seems that without a login page, the browser couldn't authenticate and produced the error. After I added a login page, I was properly redirected and everything worked fine. Older versions of [product_name] web editor would auto-create a login page, but the newer version only generates a main page by default. I hope this helps! Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users report intermittent 'Error 403: Forbidden' when accessing the [product_name] web server. The error can occur after several successful uses, and temporary fixes include clearing cookies or switching browsers. Additional complications arise from incorrect port settings, sessions not closing properly, or missing login page configurations in newer software versions. The main usability challenges involve unclear error communication, inconsistent browser compatibility, and complex server setup.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect stable and reliable web server access across browsers and sessions, with easy troubleshooting for forbidden errors. They also look for clear documentation and default settings that reduce configuration mistakes.
